Summarise cognitive interviews per item

Source: R/interview.R
summarise_interviews.Rd

summarise_interviews() rolls the coded interviews of cognitive_interview() up to one row per item: The share of interviews with a problem at each stage and at any stage, how many personas and models raised a problem, the coder's most common notes and the suggested rewordings.

Usage

summarise_interviews(x, flag = 0.3, n_notes = 3)

Arguments

x

a result of cognitive_interview().

flag

the share of interviews with a problem at which an item is flagged.

n_notes

how many notes and rewordings to keep per item.

Value

A tibble of class sc_interview_summary, one row per item, with item, statement, n, one share per stage, any, major (share of major problems), personas and models (how many raised a problem), top_stage, flagged, pretest, agreement, notes and revisions. The attribute text holds the paragraph.

Details

An item is flagged when the share of interviews with a problem at any stage is at least flag and, when there are two or more models, at least two of them raise a problem (one model alone is weaker evidence). With a pretest, agreement says whether the item was flagged by both, by the pretest only, by the interviews only, or by neither: Items flagged by both are the first to revise.

Printing the result shows a short paragraph, written by fixed rules, before the table. These are screening results: They point to items to look at in human cognitive interviews and a field test.

See also

cognitive_interview(), gg_interview()

Examples

items <- data.frame(item = c("q1", "q2"),
                    statement = c("I never don't worry.", "I keep my promises."))
iv <- cognitive_interview(sc_instrument(items), sc_model("mock"),
                          c("You are 20 years old.", "You are 70 years old."),
                          interviews = 3)
#> 12 interviews (1 model x 2 personas x 2 items x 3 interviews): 36 requests.
summarise_interviews(iv)
#> 1 of 2 items is flagged: q1 (100% of interviews, mostly comprehension).
#> These are screening results from language models: Use them to choose
#> items for cognitive interviews with real people and a field test, not
#> to replace them.
#> 
#> # A tibble: 2 × 9
#>   item  comprehension retrieval judgement response sensitivity   any models
#>   <chr>         <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl>  <int>
#> 1 q1                1         0         0        0           0     1      1
#> 2 q2                0         0         0        0           0     0      0
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: flagged <lgl>
